why: The student copies the array one element at a time instead of assigning the reference, which is the right approach. The code still has two errors: it never creates the copy array, and the bound i <= data2.length goes one index past the end and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Because the new code is not correct, it cannot be L4.

concepts.why: The answer makes no claim about int itself.
data2.length is written correctly, but the answer's reasoning is not about the length field; the bound error is levelled under off_by_one_error.
The for loop is only a vehicle for the copy, and the answer makes no separate claim about it.
i++ appears only as the standard update, with no claim about it.

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i <= data2.length; i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: It copies element by element into copy[i] in order, but it never creates copy with new and it runs past the last index.
This uses <= where < is needed (the OffByOneBound misconception), so the last pass reads data2[data2.length] and throws an exception.
The answer makes no claim about primitive types.
The bound error is already levelled under off_by_one_error.
The answer makes no claim about aliasing.
